column1: # tests/memfn/search_vocab.tsv -- THE SEARCH-FORM VOCABULARY: what text, spelled
# by a pcrec emitter, counts as a search or span-compare FORM.
# ONE PLACE. integration.md §R4.3.4 defines C17's static half as "an emitter
# spells a C12-vocabulary search form" and §10.5 defines C12 (the emitted-form
# ratchet) over "emitted-text libc search calls, table-walk loop texts and
# runcmp row texts". C12 is not built yet (it is born at R4c, §22), so this
# file is born here, at R4a, with C17, and is the vocabulary BOTH read: C12,
# when it lands, counts these classes against its ceiling instead of spelling
# a second list (lane memfnmanifest, 2026-10-05).
# INDEPENDENCE. This file names no site, no manifest row and no emitter
# function. It describes TEXT SHAPES, and C17 asks which functions spell them.
# The manifest (site_manifest.tsv) names functions and never a shape. A shape
# added here for a site the manifest lacks makes C17 fail (rule 1); a site
# the manifest lists whose text no line here recognises makes C17 fail too
# (rule 4). Neither file can quietly agree with the other.
# HOW A LINE IS APPLIED (tests/memfn/c17_lex.py): to every C string literal
# inside a file-scope definition under src/gen/ and src/enc/, with adjacent
# literals joined as the C compiler joins them and the emitter's own comments
# removed. The text is the literal's SOURCE spelling: `\n` is two characters
# and `%s`/`%d` are the emitter's format holes. Python `re`, searched (not
# anchored) in each joined literal.
# STATED LIMIT (§R4.3.4): a search spelled in a shape no line recognises
# escapes the static half until a line here learns it. Adding a line is
# ordinary C17 maintenance; removing one is how a form escapes, so a removal
# names the form it stops seeing in its commit.
# Columns (tab-separated): class, line-id, regex, what it recognises.
# class         line-id          regex
libc-search
column4: an emitted libc search or compare call whose FIRST operand is the subject, a format hole the emitter fills, or appended by the next statement (so prose such as "memchr()" and a compare of two caller-supplied names, `memcmp(cv->name, ...)`, are not search forms)

column1: table-walk
column4: a one-statement cursor loop whose condition looks the subject byte at the cursor up in a table and whose body steps the cursor (`while (pos < n && T[subject[pos]]) pos++;`); the loop is also recognised braced, the step on its own line after the indent hole (`while ((pos < n) && (T[subject[pos]])) {\n%s    pos++;\n%s}`), which is the kit's ADVANCE layout that [MEMFN] R4h's layout normalization (abi 67) made pcrec emit

column1: table-walk
column4: the same one-statement cursor walk spelled through format holes (`while (%s < %s && !%s_%s[%s[%s]]) %s++;`, THE FIND's table form, START-SET stage 1's `pcrec_emit_find`): the table, the subject and the cursor are all the caller's

column1: table-walk
column4: an emitted `while (` whose condition the literal leaves open, to be completed by a predicate another emitter call splices in (the class-run and span loops whose byte test is not theirs to spell; since M6 pcrec spells none: the VM's strided span loop, its last form outside the kit, is the kit's VMSTRIDE); the condition may carry one level of balanced parens and end inside one more open paren (`while ((%s) && (` and `while ((%s_span_cursor + %d <= %s)`, the kit's ADVANCE layout parenthesises `more` and the member, [MEMFN] R4h's layout normalization, abi 67), where the old `[^)]*$` stopped seeing the form at the first `)`

column1: runcmp
column4:
a run compare by natural-width word loads (`

_wN(base) ==

_wN("...")`)

column1: runcmp
column4: a run compare one byte position at a time against a constant, masked or exact

column1: span-compare
column4: the encoding seam's run-time span compare: the subject operand read at the walk index of a two-operand compare loop (D147 addendum 10, Q54)

column1: span-compare
column4: a COUNTED span loop opened by an emitter: a counter below a count the emitter fills, braced, its block test spelled by the next literals (the VM cursor rung's lazy rmin prefix as M6 found it, Q-R10-7; since R-12's REPLACE that prefix is the kit's VMSPAN/VMSTRIDE site and NO emitter spells this form: the line is KEPT at C12 ceiling 0 (no row) as the tripwire for a re-spelled counted loop, RULED Q-R12-6)

column1: word-skip
column4: a word-at-a-time SKIP: eight bytes loaded as one word and the loop left at the first word with any high bit set (`if (w & 0x8080808080808080ull) break;`), i.e. a scan over the byte set {0x00..0x7F} in SWAR form (the utf8 backend's `$_valid_upto` ASCII run, [UTF-VALID]; listed by R-12, Q-R12-5)
